title: Which of these expressions always give even numbers?
description: Eight expressions are sorted into always even and not always even, by taking out the factor two or by finding one example that gives an odd number. Then three new expressions that are always even are written and checked. The method is the same as the examples in the book on always even expressions.
teaching_notes: One idea: an expression is always even when the factor two can be taken out, and it is not always even when one example gives an odd number. Watch for students who call an expression always even because the examples they tried happened to be even.

video_script.why: A learner decides whether each expression is always even by taking out the factor two or by finding an odd example, then writes new always even expressions.
video_script.anchor: eight expression cards sorted into an always even box and a not always even box, as in the book
video_script.payoff_line: Five of the expressions are always even, and three are not always even.

final_answer.value: Always even: 2a + 2b, 4m + 2n, 2u − 4v, 13k − 5k, 4k × 3j. Not always even: 3g + 5h, 6m − 3n, b² + 1
final_answer.spoken: five of the expressions are always even, and three are not always even

hold_back: Always even: 2a + 2b, 4m + 2n, 2u − 4v, 13k − 5k, 4k × 3j. Not always even: 3g + 5h, 6m − 3n, b² + 1
maths_rules: 2a + 2b = 2(a + b); 4m + 2n = 2(2m + n); 2u - 4v = 2(u - 2v); each has the factor 2
3g + 5h with g = 1, h = 2: 3 x 1 = 3, 5 x 2 = 10, 3 + 10 = 13, odd; so not always even
6m - 3n with m = 1, n = 1: 6 - 3 = 3, odd; b^2 + 1 with b = 2: 4 + 1 = 5, odd
new always even: 2x + 6, 10y - 4z, 6p x q; each has the factor 2
video_script.design: One idea: take out the factor two for always even, and find one odd example for not always. Assumes the examples on always even expressions. The eight cards stay on the board and slide into the two boxes.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about expressions that give even numbers.
<bookmark mark='same'/>We will solve it the same way as the examples in your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of these eight expressions always give even numbers?

beats.on_screen: the eight cards stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the factor 2 taken out of an expression; one odd answer for a number put in

marks.factor: the factor two is lifted out of an expression card
marks.odd: one number is put in and an odd answer lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='factor'/>An expression is always even when we can take out the factor two.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>It is not always even if we find one case where it gives an odd number.

marks.given: the eight expressions are written in two rows

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, there are eight expressions with letters in them.

beats.on_screen: To find: which are always even; examples for the others; new always even expressions
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which are always even. We also give an odd example for the others, and write new ones.

marks.first: two eigh plus two b becomes two times the bracket
marks.second: four m plus two n becomes two times a bracket
marks.third: two u minus four v becomes two times a bracket

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, take out the factor two. Two eigh plus two b is two times the bracket eigh plus b.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Four m plus two n is two times the bracket two m plus n.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Two u minus four v is two times the bracket u minus two v. All three are always even.

marks.minus: thirteen k minus five k becomes eight k, then two times four k
marks.times: four k times three j becomes twelve k j, then two times six k j

narration: <bookmark mark='minus'/>Step two, tidy the other two first. Thirteen k minus five k is eight k, which is two times four k.
<bookmark mark='times'/>Four k times three j is twelve k j, which is two times six k j. Both are always even.

marks.put: one goes into g and two goes into h
marks.sum: three and ten add to thirteen and it is tagged odd

narration: <bookmark mark='put'/>Step three, try three g plus five h with g as one and h as two. Three times one is three, and five times two is ten.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Three plus ten is thirteen, which is odd. This one is not always even.

marks.six: six minus three shows three and it is tagged odd
marks.square: two squared shows four, then four plus one shows five and it is tagged odd

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step four, try six m minus three n with m and n both one. Six minus three is three, which is odd.
<bookmark mark='square'/>Try b squared plus one with b as two. Two squared is four, and four plus one is five, which is odd.

marks.new: three new cards appear, each with the factor two lit

narration: <bookmark mark='new'/>Step five, write new expressions that have the factor two. Take two x plus six, ten y minus four z, and six p times q.

marks.two: y as two and z as three give twenty minus twelve, which is eight
marks.three: p as one and q as five give thirty

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step six, put numbers back to check. With x as three, two times three plus six is twelve.
<bookmark mark='two'/>With y as two and z as three, twenty minus twelve is eight.
<bookmark mark='three'/>With p as one and q as five, six times one times five is thirty. All three are even.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Always even: 2a + 2b, 4m + 2n, 2u − 4v, 13k − 5k, 4k × 3j. Not always even: 3g + 5h, 6m − 3n, b² + 1

marks.e1: the first two cards glow in the always even box
marks.e2: the next three cards glow in the always even box
marks.n1: the last three cards glow in the not always even box

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Five of the expressions are always even, and three are not always even.
<bookmark mark='e1'/>Always even are two eigh plus two b, and four m plus two n.
<bookmark mark='e2'/>Also two u minus four v, thirteen k minus five k, and four k times three j.
<bookmark mark='n1'/>Not always even are three g plus five h, and six m minus three n. Also b squared plus one.
